questions.q: What is the core timing problem that responsible scaling frameworks are designed to address?
options: That evaluations take too long to run compared to training
That it's easier to make honest safety decisions before a powerful model already exists, since organizational pressure to ship rises once it's built
That capability thresholds can only be measured after a model is deployed publicly
That labs cannot agree on a single shared framework
questions.explain: Pre-committing to thresholds and safeguards before a triggering capability is reached is meant to counteract the pressure to ship a finished, capable model.

questions.q: What does Anthropic's ASL-3 level in its Responsible Scaling Policy represent?
options: Systems with no meaningful catastrophic risk at all
A level reserved only for models that have already caused real-world harm
Systems that substantially increase catastrophic misuse risk compared to non-AI baselines, or show low-level autonomous capabilities, requiring stronger safeguards
A level that applies exclusively to narrow, non-LLM systems
questions.explain: ASL-3 marks a substantial step up in catastrophic misuse risk or autonomous capability, triggering materially stronger deployment and security requirements.

questions.q: How does OpenAI's Preparedness Framework structure its risk assessment?
options: By assigning a single overall safety score with no category breakdown
Around Tracked Categories such as biological/chemical risk, cybersecurity, and model autonomy, each with pre- and post-mitigation risk ratings
By relying entirely on external regulators to set risk levels
By using the exact same ASL numbering system as Anthropic
questions.explain: The Preparedness Framework rates models in specific Tracked Categories, with a Safety Advisory Group reviewing ratings and recommending deployment restrictions.

questions.q: What does crossing a Critical Capability Level (CCL) trigger under DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework?
options: Immediate and permanent discontinuation of the model
A requirement for heightened evaluation and mitigation, and in later revisions, an approved safety case before broad deployment
No specific requirement; CCLs are purely descriptive, not actionable
Automatic public release of the model's full training data
questions.explain: Crossing a CCL triggers heightened scrutiny, mitigation requirements, and later framework versions require an internally approved safety case before broad deployment.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue the shared structure of these frameworks matters more than any single framework's specific threshold numbers?
options: Because the specific numbers are classified and cannot be discussed
Because all three labs describe their frameworks as living documents subject to revision, so the transferable lesson is the shared pre-commitment pattern, not any one fixed threshold
Because the frameworks have no meaningful differences worth noting
Because thresholds are set by international law rather than by the labs themselves
questions.explain: All three frameworks are explicitly revisable; what transfers across labs and over time is the structural bet of pre-committing thresholds and safeguards, not the exact current numbers.
